newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Largest-cap firms drive Moroccan bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Largest-cap firms drive Moroccan bourse higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended the week up 3.5 percent Friday, lifted by the largest-capitalisation firms and heavy trading in privatisation bonds, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 620.01, up from 598.64 last Friday.

"During the week, traders were interested in shares of largest-capitalisation companies...Investors also rushed to buy privatisation bonds ahead of new flotations on the bourse," a broker at the Casablanca-based Safa bourse said.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private holding, closed at 781 dirhams, up from 750 a week earlier. ONA Group has a market capitalisation of more than 13 billion dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the country's second conglomerate, which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, closed at 705 dirhams, down from 717.
Oil refinery Samir closed at 281 dirhams, unchanged from last week.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique closed at 223 dirhams, up from 209. Some 43,000 BNDE shares were traded on the official market during the week.
Leasing firm Maroc-Leasing, which was listed on the bourse in February, closed at 410 dirhams, up from 359.
Credit firm rose 32 dirhams to close at 742 dirhams.

The off market on Friday saw only small volumes traded. The most significant was in cement firm Lafarge Ciments, with 1,650 shares, a stockbroker at ABN-AMRO Finance said. Volume totalled 15.8 million dirhams, against 47.6 million last Friday, he said.
On the official market, volume was 116 million dirhams, against 66.3 million last Friday.
Friday's offical market was made up of 303 deals involving 108,218 shares with a total value of 100.8 dirhams, and 26 deals involving 6,330 privatisation bonds valued at 15.7 million dirhams.
